974.exampleEn: We were disappointed that the outdoor concert was canceled due to rain.
974.shortcutEs: Decepcionado (De- Down + Ception Expectation — twin of "Disappointed / Deceived"!) | Desilusionado (Twin of "Disillusioned" — shattered illusion!) = Disappointed!
974.shortcutHi: Niraash (Nir- Without + Aasha Hope — Tamil நிராசை Niraasai! = Zero hope!) / Maayoos (Arabic loan — drooping face whispering "My-use is lost" in gloom!) = Disappointed!

975.exampleEn: The customer was very satisfied with the prompt repair service.
975.shortcutHi: Khush ≈ Spoken Tamil குஷ் / குஷி (Khushi = Happy/Pleased!) → Warm inner smile of being totally satisfied = Satisfied (Khush)!

trans.es: 1. Deep feeling: Emoción / sentimiento | 2. Temporary state of mind: Estado de ánimo / humor
trans.hi: 1. Deep feeling: Bhavna / jazbaat | 2. Temporary state of mind: Mizaaj / mann

976.exampleEn: Music has the unique power to express deep human emotion.
976.shortcutEs:
1. Feeling: Emoción (Twin of "Emotion"!) | Sentimiento (Twin of "Sentiment" feeling!) = Emotion!
2. Mood: Estado de ánimo (Estado State + de Ánimo "Animation/Mind"!) | Humor (Twin of "Humor / Mood"!) = Mood!
976.shortcutHi:
1. Feeling: Bhavna (Tamil பாவனை Bhaavanai = Inner emotion/feeling!) / Jazbaat (Arabic plural of Jazba = Deep stirring passions!) = Emotion!
2. Mood: Mizaaj (Arabic temper of mind — classic "Aapke mizaaj kaise hain?" = How is your mood?) / Mann (Tamil மனம் Manam = Mind/Heart!) = Mood!
976.hiDevanagari: 1. Deep feeling: Bhavna / jazbaat | 2. Temporary state of mind: Mizaaj / mann

977.exampleEn: The birth of their healthy baby brought immense joy to the whole family.
977.shortcutEs: Alegría (Latin Alacer Lively/Brisk — root of musical "Allegro"!) | Gozo (Latin Gaudium Gladness — root of "Gaudy / Rejoice"!) = Joy / Delight!
977.shortcutHi: Khushi (Persian Khush Glad/Happy [Tamil குஷி Khushi = Joy!] + -i Quality = Gladness!) = Joy / Delight!

978.exampleEn: Time and community support help heal deep personal sorrow.
978.shortcutHi: Dukh (Sanskrit Duhkha [Tamil துக்கம் Thukkam = Sorrow!]!) / Gham (Arabic Ghamm Dark cloud weighing on chest!) = Sorrow / Grief!

979.exampleEn: He managed to control his sudden flash of rage and stayed silent.
979.shortcutEs: Furia (Twin of English "Fury"!) | Rabia (Boiling mad "Rabies / Rabid" temper!) | Cólera (Hot red-faced bile "Cholera / Choler" anger!) = Rage!
979.shortcutHi: Ghussa ≈ Spoken Tamil குஸ்ஸா — flaring crimson anger boiling up inside chest = Rage (Ghussa)!

980.exampleEn: The loud explosion filled the crowded street with sudden terror.
980.shortcutEs: Pánico (Twin of English "Panic"!) | Terror (Twin of English "Terror"!) = Paralyzing fear = Terror / Panic!
980.shortcutHi: Behad darr (Be-had Without Limit + Darr Dread/Fear!) / Ghabraahat (From Ghabraana = Heart pounding frantically in panic!) = Terror / Panic!

981.exampleEn: Regular physical exercise and proper sleep help reduce daily anxiety.
981.shortcutEs: Ansiedad (Twin of English "Anxiety"!) | Estrés (Twin of English "Stress"!) = Restless worry = Anxiety / Stress!
981.shortcutHi: Tension (English loan "Tension" tight chest worry) / Chinta (Tamil சிந்தை / சிந்தனை Chinthai = Deep anxious thought!) = Anxiety / Stress!

982.exampleEn: Parents watched with great pride as their daughter received her degree.
982.shortcutEs:
1. Self-respect: Orgullo (High-held chin of honor — picture marching tall with an "Aura-Glow"!) = Pride!
2. Arrogance: Soberbia (Latin Superbia = "Super-Superior" haughtiness!) | Orgullo (Swollen chest puffing "Aura-Glow" arrogance!) = Arrogance!
982.shortcutHi:
1. Self-respect: Garv (Tamil கர்வம் Garvam = Pride! → 100% same word!) = Pride!
2. Arrogance: Ghamand (Swollen stiff head boasting "Go-Command!" above everyone!) = Arrogance!

trans.es: 1. Warm fondness: Cariño / afecto | 2. Intense fervor: Pasión
trans.hi: 1. Warm fondness: Lagav / pyaar | 2. Intense fervor: Josh / deewanapan

983.tamil: 1. பாசம் / அன்பு (Warm fondness) / 2. தீவிர ஆர்வம் / வெறி (Intense fervor)
983.exampleEn: The grandmother showed warm affection by hugging each grandchild gently.
983.shortcutEs:
1. Fondness: Cariño (Tender sweet-heart "Caring"!) | Afecto (Twin of "Affection"!) = Affection!
2. Fervor: Pasión (Twin of English "Passion"!) = Passion!
983.shortcutHi:
1. Fondness: Lagav (From Lagna = Attached heart bond!) / Pyaar (Tamil பிரியம் Priyam ≈ Pyaar = Love!) = Affection!
2. Fervor: Josh (Arabic fiery spirit — remember famous "How's the Josh?"!) / Deewanapan (Deewana Crazy-devoted + -pan State!) = Passion!
983.hiDevanagari: 1. Warm fondness: Lagav / pyaar | 2. Intense fervor: Josh / deewanapan

984.exampleEn: The sight of rotten spoiled food caused strong immediate disgust.
984.shortcutEs: Asco (Nauseating revulsion — root related to repulsive bile that turns the stomach!) = Disgust!

985.exampleEn: Professional counseling and supportive friends help overcome deep
985.shortcutEs: Depresión (Twin of "Depression"!) | Bajón (From Bajar Go down + -ón Big = Heavy emotional crash/drop!) = Depression!
985.shortcutHi: Gehri udaasi (Gehri Deep + Udaasi Melancholy sadness — dark sunken blues!) / Depression (English loan "Depression") = Depression!

986.exampleEn: The new volunteers joined the charity project with tremendous enthusiasm.
986.shortcutEs: Entusiasmo (Twin of English "Enthusiasm"!) | Ganas (Burning urge to score "Gains" — phrase "Tengo ganas!" = I'm pumped!) = Enthusiasm!
986.shortcutHi: Josh ≈ Electrifying fire inside belly (Think famous slogan "How's the Josh?! High sir!") = Enthusiasm (Josh)!

987.exampleEn: Learning a foreign language fluently requires daily practice and patience.
987.shortcutHi: Sabr (Arabic Sabr Steady restraint — root behind famous proverb "Sabr ka phal meetha"!) = Patience!

988.exampleEn: Firefighters display remarkable courage when rescuing people from burning

trans.es: 1. Emotional jolt: Conmoción / susto | 2. Electrical: Descarga eléctrica / choque
trans.hi: 1. Emotional jolt: Sadma / jhatka | 2. Electrical: Current / bijli ka jhatka

989.tamil: 1. மன அதிர்ச்சி (Emotional jolt) / 2. மின்சார அதிர்ச்சி (Electrical shock)
989.exampleEn: The sudden unexpected news came as a complete shock to everyone.
989.shortcutEs:
1. Emotional jolt: Conmoción (Twin of "Commotion" shock!) | Susto (Sudden heart-stopping scare!) = Shock!
2. Electrical: Descarga eléctrica (Electric "Discharge"!) | Choque (Twin of "Shock"!) = Electric Shock!
989.shortcutHi:
1. Emotional jolt: Sadma (Heavy emotional blow — famous classic movie "Sadma"!) / Jhatka (Sudden violent snap jerk — "Jolt-ka"!) = Shock!
2. Electrical: Current (English loan "Current") / Bijli ka jhatka (Bijli Electricity + Jhatka Jolt!) = Electric Shock!
989.hiDevanagari: 1. Emotional jolt: Sadma / jhatka | 2. Electrical: Current / bijli ka jhatka

990.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues
990.exampleEn: It was very nice meeting you at the cultural conference yesterday.
990.shortcutEs: Simpático (Twin of "Sympathetic / Warm"!) | Amable (Twin of "Amiable" kind!) | Agradable (Twin of "Agreeable / Pleasant"!) = Nice / Friendly!
990.shortcutHi: Milansaar (From Milna Meet/Mix + -saar Flowing = Easy-mixing!) / Achha (Clean wholesome good — Tamil நன்று!) / Pyaara (From Pyaar Love = Sweet/Lovable!) = Nice / Friendly!

991.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues
991.exampleEn: Interrupting people while they speak is very rude and disrespectful.
991.shortcutEs: Grosero (Grueso Thick/Coarse + -ero = Unpolished blunt manners!) | Maleducado (Mal Badly + Educado Raised!) = Rude!

992.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues
992.exampleEn: Making careless mistakes without reading instructions is completely stupid.
992.shortcutHi: Bewaqoof (Persian Be- Without + Arabic Wuquf Sense!) / Moorkh (Sanskrit Murkha [Tamil மூர்க்கன்] Fool!) / Pagal (Crazy-headed!) = Stupid / Foolish!

993.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues
993.exampleEn: The hardworking farmers worked in the fields from dawn until dusk.
993.shortcutEs: Trabajador / trabajadora ≈ From Trabajo ("Travel-Job" work) → Tireless male or female Hardworking pro!

994.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues
994.exampleEn: Cheating on an examination is completely dishonest and strictly forbidden.
994.shortcutEs: Deshonesto (Des- Dis- + Honesto Honest!) | Tramposo (Sets a crooked "Trap" — card cheater!) = Dishonest!
994.shortcutHi: Be-imaan (Be- Without + Imaan Faith/Conscience = Corrupt!) / Jhootha (Built on Jhooth Falsehood = Spoken lie!) = Dishonest!

995.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues
995.exampleEn: Despite his huge global success, the famous scientist remained very humble.
995.shortcutEs: Humilde (Twin of English "Humble"!) | Modesto (Twin of English "Modest"!) = Down-to-earth = Humble / Modest!
995.shortcutHi: Seedha-saadha (Seedha Straight/Unbent + Saadha Tamil சாதாரண Simple = Plain & unpretentious!) = Humble / Modest!

996.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues
996.exampleEn: Running away and leaving your friends behind in danger is cowardly.
996.shortcutEs: Cobarde ≈ Literally twin of English "Coward / Cowardly" — hiding behind fear = Cowardly (Cobarde)!
996.shortcutHi: Darpok (Built on Darr Fear — trembling chicken hiding at tiny noises!) / Buzdil (Persian Buz Goat + Dil Heart = Scared goat-heart!) = Cowardly!

997.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues
997.exampleEn: The generous donor gave scholarships to fifty deserving university students.
997.shortcutEs: Generoso / generosa ≈ Open hands freely sharing bread and coins! = Generous!

998.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues

trans.es: 1. Avaricious for money/food: Codicioso / avaro | 2. Self-centered: Egoísta
trans.hi: 1. Avaricious for money/food: Laalchi | 2. Self-centered: Khudgarz

998.exampleEn: The greedy merchant kept all the profits and shared nothing with workers.
998.shortcutEs:
1. Money/food hungry: Codicioso (Obsessed with "Coveting" loot!) | Avaro (Root of English "Avarice"!) = Greedy!
2. Self-centered: Egoísta (Obsessed with "Ego" me-me-me!) = Selfish!
998.shortcutHi:
1. Money/food hungry: Laalchi (Built on Laalach = Drooling greed for coins!) = Greedy!
2. Self-centered: Khudgarz (Persian Khud Self + Garz Need = Only cares for own needs!) = Selfish!
998.hiDevanagari: 1. Avaricious for money/food: Laalchi | 2. Self-centered: Khudgarz

999.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues
999.exampleEn: He was too stubborn to admit that his navigation directions were wrong.
999.shortcutEs: Terco (Unbending stiff neck!) | Testarudo (Testa Hard Head + -udo = Hard-headed!) | Tozudo (Big-head obstinate!) = Stubborn!
999.shortcutHi: Ziddi (Arabic Zidd Contrarian persistence + -i!) / Adiyal (Adna Plant feet & refuse to budge!) = Stubborn!

1000.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues
1000.exampleEn: Creative artists find beauty in simple everyday objects and scenes.
1000.shortcutEs: Creativo / creativa ≈ Artist's colorful palette sparking fresh inventions! = Creative!
1000.shortcutHi: Nayi soch wala ≈ Nayi (New) + Soch (Thought/Idea) + Wala (Person with) → Original thinker → Creative (Nayi soch wala)!

1001.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues
1001.exampleEn: The clumsy waiter accidentally dropped a tray of clean glasses.

1002.category: Category 49: Personality, Character Traits & Human Virtues
1002.exampleEn: She is a reliable colleague who always completes projects on time.
1002.shortcutEs: Confiable (Someone you can "Confide" in safely!) | Responsable (Twin of English "Responsible"!) = Reliable / Responsible!
1002.shortcutHi: Bharosemand (Bharosa Trust + -mand Full of = Trustworthy!) / Zimmedaar (Zimma Duty + -daar Holder = Responsible!) = Reliable / Responsible!

trans.es: 1. Grown-up mindset: Maduro / madura | 2. Childish: Inmaduro / inmadura

1003.exampleEn: She showed a mature attitude by discussing the disagreement calmly.
1003.shortcutEs:
1. Grown-up: Maduro / madura (Twin of English "Mature"!) = Mature!
2. Childish: Inmaduro / inmadura (In- Not + Maduro Mature!) = Immature!
1003.shortcutHi:
1. Grown-up: Samajhdaar (Samajh Understanding + -daar Possessing = Wise!) = Mature!
2. Childish: Bachkana (Built directly on Bachha Kid/Child = Acting like a kid!) = Immature!

1004.exampleEn: The headmaster has very strict rules regarding punctuality and discipline.
1004.shortcutEs: Estricto / estricta (Twin of English "Strict"!) | Severo (Twin of English "Severe" stern rulebook!) = Strict!
1004.shortcutHi: Sakht (Persian hard stone — rigid unbending discipline!) / Kadak (Crisp crackling sternness — think biting strict drill sergeant "Kadak" voice!) = Strict!

1005.exampleEn: Treat sensitive skin gently using pure natural fragrance-free soaps.
1005.shortcutEs: Sensible ≈ False friend alert! Looks like "Sensible", actually means emotionally "Sensitive" (easily moved to tears!) = Sensitive (Sensible)!
1005.shortcutHi: Naazuk (Persian delicate glass petal — fragile & easily hurt!) / Jazbaati (Built on Jazbaat Emotion — wears heart on sleeve!) = Sensitive!

1006.exampleEn: Be gentle and patient when holding the tiny baby kitten.
1006.shortcutHi: Naram (Persian soft pillowy feather touch — gentle voice & hands!) / Meetha (Sweet honey-soft tone without sharp bite — Tamil மதுரம்!) = Gentle!

trans.es: 1. Undomesticated animal/nature: Salvaje / silvestre | 2. Uncontrolled behavior: Loco / descontrolado
trans.hi: 1. Undomesticated animal/nature: Jangli | 2. Uncontrolled behavior: Bekaboo / mast

1007.exampleEn: Never approach dangerous wild animals in their natural forest habitat.
1007.shortcutEs:
1. Untamed: Salvaje (Twin of English "Savage" jungle beast!) | Silvestre (Growing in forest "Sylvan" wild!) = Wild!
2. Uncontrolled: Loco (Wild "Loco" frenzy!) | Descontrolado (Des- Out of + Control!) = Wild!
1007.shortcutHi:
1. Untamed: Jangli (Built on Jangal = Born untamed inside the Jungle!) = Wild!
2. Uncontrolled: Bekaboo (Be- Without + Kaboo Control!) / Mast (Persian Mast Intoxicated — Spoken Tamil மஸ்த் = Carefree wild!) = Uncontrolled / Wild!
1007.hiDevanagari: 1. Undomesticated animal/nature: Jangli | 2. Uncontrolled behavior: Bekaboo / mast

1008.exampleEn: Practice your speech thoroughly so that you feel confident on stage.
1008.shortcutEs: Seguro (de sí mismo) (Seguro Secure + de sí mismo in oneself!) | Confiado (Full of self-"Confidence"!) = Confident!
1008.shortcutHi: Confident (English loan "Confident" standing tall) / Pakka (Solid baked brick — Tamil பக்கா Pakkaa = Rock-solid sure!) = Confident!

1009.exampleEn: A loyal friend stays by your side even in difficult times.
1009.shortcutEs: Leal (Twin of English "Loyal"!) | Fiel (Same Latin root as "Fidelity" faithfulness!) | Sincero (Twin of "Sincere"!) = Loyal / Sincere!
1009.shortcutHi: Wafadaar (Wafa Faith/Fidelity + -daar Holder — loyal friend who never deserts!) / Sachha (Built on Sach Truth = Genuine sincere heart!) = Loyal / Sincere!

1010.exampleEn: Treating helpless animals without food and shelter is extremely cruel.
1010.shortcutHi: Zaalim (Arabic root Zulm = Tyrant cruelty — classic Bollywood villain title "Zaalim"!) / Beraham (Be- Without + Raham Mercy = Heartless!) = Cruel!

1011.exampleEn: Nobody likes working with an arrogant person who dismisses other people's
1011.shortcutEs: Arrogante (Twin of "Arrogant"!) | Creído (From Creer "Credo/Credit" = Conceited ego believing he is king!) | Prepotente (Pre- Over + Potent Power = Overbearing ego!) = Arrogant!
1011.shortcutHi: Ghamandi ≈ Built on Ghamand (Swollen nose-in-air pride — strutting around puffing chest!) = Arrogant (Ghamandi)!

1012.exampleEn: We enjoyed a quiet and peaceful afternoon walking by the lake.
1012.shortcutHi: Shaant (Tamil சாந்தம் Shaantham = Calm! → Exact same ancient root!) / Pur-sukoon (Pur Full of + Sukoon Serene peace!) = Peaceful!

1013.exampleEn: Her cheerful smile and warm greeting brightened everyone's morning.
1013.shortcutEs: Alegre (Bright musical "Allegro" beat!) | Animado (Twin of "Animated / Full of spirit"!) | Risueño (Built on Risa Smile/Laugh = Always smiling!) = Cheerful!
1013.shortcutHi: Khush-mizaaj (Khush Happy + Mizaaj Mood = Sunny disposition!) / Zindadil (Zinda Alive + Dil Heart = Lively heart!) = Cheerful!

1014.exampleEn: The dark rainy weather created a quiet and gloomy atmosphere indoors.
1014.shortcutEs: Sombrío (Wrapped in dark Sombra shadow — root of "Somber"!) | Apagado (From Apagar Extinguish — root "Pacify/Put out flame"!) | Decaído (De- Down + Caído Fallen spirits!) = Gloomy!
1014.shortcutHi: Udaas ≈ Heavy downcast sigh — drooping shoulders lost in gray sadness (think classic "Udaas shaam" = gloomy evening)! = Gloomy (Udaas)!

1015.exampleEn: The energetic puppies ran around the yard without stopping to rest.
1015.shortcutEs: Enérgico (Twin of "Energetic"!) | Activo (Twin of "Active"!) | Lleno de energía (Literally "Full of Energy"!) = Energetic!
1015.shortcutHi: Chust (Snappy crisp briskness — classic pair "Chust-Durust" = Fit & brisk!) / Phurteela (Built on Phurti = Lightning agility bursting with zip!) = Energetic!

1016.exampleEn: Be cautious when investing money in unverified internet schemes.
1016.shortcutEs: Precavido (Pre- Before + Cav- Beware/Careful — spotting danger ahead!) | Cauteloso (Twin of English "Cautious"!) = Cautious!
1016.shortcutHi: Dhyaan rakhne wala ≈ Compound: Dhyaan (Attention/Focus — Tamil தியானம் Dhiyaanam) + Rakhne wala (Keeper) = Watchful & careful = Cautious!

1017.exampleEn: Taking the lead in times of crisis requires bold and decisive action.
1017.shortcutEs: Audaz (Twin of English "Audacious"!) | Atrevido (Daring rebel — thinks "I Dare!") | Valiente (Twin of "Valiant"!) = Bold!
1017.shortcutHi: Nidar (Ni- Without + Darr Fear = Fearless!) / Himmati (Built on Himmat Courage = Gutsy!) = Bold!

trans.es: 1. Free from guilt: Inocente | 2. Naive/pure: Ingenuo / inocente
trans.hi: 1. Free from guilt: Be-kasoor | 2. Naive/pure: Masoom / bhola

1018.exampleEn: The little child looked up with wide, innocent, and trusting eyes.
1018.shortcutEs:
1. Not guilty: Inocente (Twin of English "Innocent"!) = Innocent!
2. Naive: Ingenuo (Twin of English "Ingenuous / Naive"!) | Inocente (Pure-hearted child!) = Naive!
1018.shortcutHi:
1. Not guilty: Be-kasoor (Be- Without + Kasoor Fault — zero blame!) = Innocent!
2. Naive: Masoom (Arabic loan — pure wide-eyed childlike innocence!) / Bhola (Sweet trusting village simplicity — remember warm nickname "Bhola-bhala"!) = Naive / Pure!
1018.hiDevanagari: 1. Free from guilt: Be-kasoor | 2. Naive/pure: Masoom / bhola

1019.exampleEn: The small coastal town has historic streets and charming waterfront cafes.
1019.shortcutEs: Encantador (Casts a magical "Enchanting" spell!) | Seductor (Twin of English "Seductive / Alluring"!) = Charming!
1019.shortcutHi: Pyaara (From Pyaar Love — irresistibly sweet!) / Dil jeetne wala (Dil Heart + Jeetne wala Winner/Capturer = Stealing every heart!) = Charming!

1020.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions

trans.es: Reírse entre dientes / soltar una risita

1020.exampleEn: He chuckled quietly while reading the funny comic strip in the paper.
1020.shortcutEs: Reírse entre dientes (Reír Laugh + entre Dientes between teeth — muffled giggle!) | Soltar una risita (Soltar Let slip + Risita Tiny laugh!) = Chuckle / Giggle!
1020.shortcutHi: Dabi hasi hansna (Dabi Pressed-down/Muffled + Hasi Laugh + Hansna Laugh!) / Khilkhilana (Bubbly open laughter sounding like crystal bells "Khil-Khil!") = Chuckle / Giggle!

1021.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions
1021.exampleEn: She wept with joy upon hearing that her missing brother was found safe.
1021.shortcutEs: Llorar (Latin Plorare Cry aloud [Implore / Deplore]!) + a lágrima viva (With streaming live tears!) = Weep!
1021.shortcutHi: Phoot-phoot kar rona (Phootna Burst open like a dam + Rona Cry = Sob openly!) = Weep!

1022.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions

trans.es: Fruncir el ceño / poner mala cara

1022.exampleEn: The teacher frowned when looking at the untidy and incomplete homework.
1022.shortcutEs: Fruncir el ceño / poner mala cara ≈ Fruncir (Frown/Scrunch brow) + Ceño (Eyebrow/Scowl) = Frown / Scowl!
1022.shortcutHi: Moonh banana ≈ Moonh (Face/Mouth) + Banana (Make) → Literally "make a sour face" → Frown / Scowl (Moonh banana)!

1023.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions
1023.exampleEn: Nod your head clearly if you understand and agree with the plan.
1023.shortcutEs: Asentir con la cabeza ≈ Asentir (Twin of English "Assent" Agree) + con la Cabeza (with head) = Nod!
1023.shortcutHi: Haan mein sir hilana ≈ Haan mein (In "Yes") + Sir (Head) + Hilana (Tilt up & down) = Nod!

1024.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions
1024.exampleEn: He just shrugged his shoulders when asked about the lost keys.

1025.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions

trans.es: 1. Hand gesture: Saludar con la mano / agitar | 2. Water swell: Ola / onda
trans.hi: 1. Hand gesture: Haath hilana | 2. Water swell: Lehar / tarang

1025.exampleEn: Wave goodbye to your grandparents as the train leaves the station.
1025.shortcutEs:
1. Hand gesture: Saludar con la mano (Saludar Salute/Greet + Mano Hand!) | Agitar ("Agitate" wave!) = Wave!
2. Ocean swell: Ola (Famous stadium cheer "La Ola!") | Onda (Water "Undulation"!) = Sea Wave!
1025.shortcutHi:
1. Hand gesture: Haath hilana (Haath Hand + Hilana Shake/Swing!) = Wave Hand!
2. Ocean swell: Lehar (Tamil அலை / லஹரி Lahari = Rising wave!) / Tarang (Tamil தரங்கம் Tharangam = Wave!) = Wave!
1025.hiDevanagari: 1. Hand gesture: Haath hilana | 2. Water swell: Lehar / tarang

1026.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions
1026.exampleEn: It is considered rude to stare at strangers in public transport.
1026.shortcutEs: Mirar fijamente (Look fixedly!) | Clavar la vista (Clavar Nail/Pin + la Vista Sight — lock eyes!) = Stare / Gaze!
1026.shortcutHi: Ghoorna (Heavy wide-eyed glares!) / Taakna (Peer steadily!) / Nigaah jamana (Plant gaze firmly!) = Stare / Gaze!

1027.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions

trans.es: Echar un vistazo / mirar de reojo

1027.exampleEn: He glanced quickly at his wristwatch to check the remaining time.
1027.shortcutEs: Echar un vistazo (Echar Cast + Vista View = Quick eye-toss!) | Mirar de reojo (Mirar Look + de Re-ojo from side-eye!) = Glance!
1027.shortcutHi: Jhalak dekhna ≈ Jhalak (Split-second shimmering flash — famous show "Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa"!) + Dekhna (See) = Quick peek = Glance!

1028.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions

trans.es: 1. Involuntary eye close: Parpadear | 2. One-eye signal: Guiñar el ojo
trans.hi: 1. Involuntary eye close: Palkein jhapkana | 2. One-eye signal: Aankh maarna

1028.exampleEn: Blink your eyes a few times to clear the dust out safely.
1028.shortcutEs:
1. Involuntary eye close: Parpadear ≈ From Párpado ("Pop-Lid" eyelid) → Flutter your eyelids = Blink (Parpadear)!
2. One-eye signal: Guiñar el ojo ≈ Wink with your Ojo (Eye = Wink)!
1028.shortcutHi:
1. Involuntary eye close: Palkein jhapkana ≈ Palkein (Eyelids) + Jhapkana (Snap-shut/flicker) = Blink / Wink!
2. One-eye signal: Aankh maarna ≈ Aankh (Eye) + Maarna (Strike/Flash) → Flash one eye = Wink (Aankh maarna)!
1028.hiDevanagari: 1. Involuntary eye close: Palkein jhapkana | 2. One-eye signal: Aankh maarna

1029.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions
1029.exampleEn: She sighed with relief after finishing the difficult three-hour examination.
1029.shortcutEs: Suspirar / suspiro ≈ Notice "Spire / Respire" → Verb & Noun for letting out a long wistful breath = Sigh!
1029.shortcutHi: Aah bharna / thandi saans lena ≈ Aah (Saying "Ahh!" exhale) + Bharna (Fill/Heave a sigh) = Sigh!

1030.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions
1030.exampleEn: The audience gasped in shock when the magician vanished suddenly.
1030.shortcutEs: Jadear (Hear breathless runner puffing "Hah-Day-Air!" needing oxygen!) | Quedarse sin aliento (Quedarse Be left + sin Aliento without breath!) = Gasp!
1030.shortcutHi: Achanak saans kheenchna (Achanak Suddenly + Saans Breath + Kheenchna Pull in!) / Haanpna (Echoes chest heaving "Haaph!-Haaph!" panting after sprinting stairs!) = Gasp!

1031.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions
1031.exampleEn: The injured player groaned in pain while holding his sprained ankle.
1031.shortcutEs: Gemir (Latin Gemere Moan/Sigh!) | Quejarse (Latin Quassare Break out in aching groans + -se!) = Groan!
1031.shortcutHi: Karahana (Moan in deep ache!) / Dard bhari aawaaz nikalna (Let out pain-filled voice!) = Groan!

1032.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions
1032.exampleEn: He snores loudly whenever he sleeps flat on his back.
1032.shortcutEs: Roncar / ronquido ≈ Loud saw-buzzing "Roar-Car" vibration — both verb & sound noun for Snore!
1032.shortcutHi: Kharraate lena ≈ Onomatopoeia "Kharrr-Kharrr!" snoring sound → Loud night Snore (Kharraate lena)!

1033.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions
1033.exampleEn: Put on a warm coat before you start to shiver in the freezing wind.
1033.shortcutEs: Temblar (Teeth-chattering tremor!) | Tiritar (Onomatopoeia "Ti-ti-ti" teeth clicking in snow!) = Shiver / Tremble!
1033.shortcutHi: Kaampna ≈ 100% same root as Tamil கம்பம் (Kampam = Tremble / Shiver!)!

1034.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions
1034.exampleEn: She blushed with embarrassment when everyone sang happy birthday to her.
1034.shortcutEs: Sonrojarse (Built on Rojo Red = Turning rosy cheeked!) | Ponerse rojo (Ponerse Become + Rojo Red!) = Blush!
1034.shortcutHi: Sharma kar laal hona ≈ Sharma kar (Feeling Sharm shyness) + Laal (Red face!) + Hona (Become) = Turn shyly red = Blush!

1035.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions
1035.exampleEn: Chew your food thoroughly so you do not accidentally choke on it.
1035.shortcutEs: Atragantarse (A- + Tragar Swallow = Swallowed stuck inside throat!) | Asfixiarse (Twin of English "Asphyxiate"!) = Choke!
1035.shortcutHi: Gala ghutna (Gala Throat + Ghutna Squeeze/Suffocate!) / Phanda lagna (Compound: Phanda Tight noose loop + Lagna Catch windpipe!) = Choke!

1036.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions
1036.exampleEn: Kneel down on the soft rug to tie your child's shoelaces easily.
1036.shortcutEs: Arrodillarse (A- To + Rodilla Knee [Little wheel Rotella] + -se!) | Hincarse (Fincar Plant knee firmly!) = Kneel!
1036.shortcutHi: Ghutne tekna (Ghutna Knee + Tekna Prop/Plant down on floor!) = Kneel!

1037.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions

trans.hi: Jhuk kar salaam karna / namaste karna

1037.exampleEn: Bow respectfully when greeting the temple elders in traditional culture.
1037.shortcutEs: Inclinarse (Twin of "Incline" bend torso forward!) | Hacer una reverencia (Literally "Make a Reverence" royal bow!) = Bow!
1037.shortcutHi: Jhuk kar salaam karna (Jhuk kar Bending + Salaam Greet) / Namaste karna (Compound: Sanskrit Namah Reverent bow + te To you!) = Bow!
1037.hiDevanagari: Jhuk kar salaam karna / namaste karna

1038.category: Category 51: Facial Expressions, Micro-Gestures & Body Reactions

trans.es: 1. Rest against: Apoyarse / recargarse | 2. Slant/incline: Inclinarse
trans.hi: 1. Rest against: Sahara lena / tek lagana | 2. Slant/incline: Jhukna

1038.exampleEn: Do not lean against the glass railing on the high balcony.
1038.shortcutEs:
1. Rest against: Apoyarse (Latin Ad-podiare = Rest foot/weight on "Podium / Support"!) | Recargarse (Re- + Cargar Cargo/Load weight onto a wall!) = Lean!
2. Slant: Inclinarse (Twin of "Incline" slant angle!) = Incline / Lean!
1038.shortcutHi:
1. Rest against: Sahara lena (Sahara Support + Lena Take!) / Tek lagana (Tek Prop-stick + Lagana Rest against!) = Lean Against!
2. Slant: Jhukna (Bend weight sideways — pair with Jhuk kar Bowing forward at a tilt!) = Lean / Slant!
1038.hiDevanagari: 1. Rest against: Sahara lena / tek lagana | 2. Slant/incline: Jhukna

1039.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1039.exampleEn: He slapped the annoying mosquito that landed on his bare arm.
1039.shortcutEs: Abofetear (Related to "Buffet" strike!) | Dar una cachetada (Dar Give + Cachete Cheek blow!) = Slap!
1039.shortcutHi: Thappad maarna (Echoes crisp flat palm "Thap!" sound + Maarna Hit!) / Chaanta maarna (Sharper stinging "Chaat!" cheek sting!) = Slap!

1040.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures

trans.es: 1. Fist strike: Dar un puñetazo / trompada | 2. Hole maker: Perforar / ponchar
trans.hi: 1. Fist strike: Ghoosa maarna | 2. Hole maker: Chhed karna

1040.exampleEn: The boxer threw a powerful punch at the heavy leather training bag.
1040.shortcutEs:
1. Fist strike: Dar un puñetazo (Compound: Dar Give + Puño Fist — same root as "Pugilist"!) | Trompada (From Trompa "Trumpet" — knockout blow!) = Punch!
2. Hole maker: Perforar (Twin of "Perforate"!) | Ponchar (Twin of "Punch" tickets!) = Punch Hole!
1040.shortcutHi:
1. Fist strike: Ghoosa maarna (Knuckled Ghoosa fist slam + Maarna Hit!) = Punch!
2. Hole maker: Chhed karna (Chhed Round hole + Karna Make = Bore hole!) = Punch Hole!
1040.hiDevanagari: 1. Fist strike: Ghoosa maarna | 2. Hole maker: Chhed karna

1041.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1041.exampleEn: Do not tickle the baby too much or she will start hiccuping.
1041.shortcutEs: Hacer cosquillas (Hacer Make + expressive Cosquillas Light rib-prickles -> laughter!) = Tickle!

1042.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1042.exampleEn: He smiled and tried to flirt playfully with the charming girl at the party.
1042.shortcutEs: Coquetear (Twin of English "Coquet / Coquette"!) | Ligar (From Ligare "Ligament / Link" = tying romantic sparks!) = Flirt!
1042.shortcutHi: Line maarna (Famous Hindi idiom literally "Throw a line"!) / Meethi baatein karna (Meethi Sweet + Baatein Talk = Charming chatter!) = Flirt!

1043.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1043.exampleEn: Give your mother a warm hug when arriving back home from college.
1043.shortcutEs: Abrazar / abrazo ≈ Built directly on Brazo (Arm — wrap both "Brazos" arms around someone = same root as "Embrace"!) = Hug!
1043.shortcutHi: Gale lagana (Gale Neck + Lagana Pull close!) / Jhappi paana (Iconic joyful Bollywood warmth: "Jaadu ki Jhappi" = Magic Hug!) = Hug!

1044.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1044.exampleEn: She gave her sleeping child a gentle goodnight kiss on the forehead.

1045.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1045.exampleEn: Allow me to introduce my new work colleague to the department team.
1045.shortcutEs: Presentar (a alguien) ≈ Politely bringing two strangers face to face ("Present" a friend!) = Introduce!

1046.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1046.exampleEn: Greet every classroom teacher with a polite smile and good morning.
1046.shortcutEs: Saludar (Twin of English "Salute" — wish health Salud!) | Dar la bienvenida (Bien Well + Venida Coming = Welcome!) = Greet!
1046.shortcutHi: Salaam karna (Salaam Peace greeting + Karna Do!) / Namaste karna (Folded-palm Hindu/Indian welcome!) = Greet!

1047.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1047.exampleEn: They decided to marry in a quiet private ceremony next spring.
1047.shortcutHi: Shaadi karna ≈ From Shaadi (Wedding) → Tie the knot = Marry (Shaadi karna)!

1048.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1048.exampleEn: The couple decided to divorce peacefully after five years of separation.
1048.shortcutEs: Divorciarse de / divorcio ≈ Legally splitting one household into two ("Di-" = Two parts!) = Divorce!
1048.shortcutHi: Talaq lena ≈ Talaq (Spoken Tamil தலாக் = Legal Divorce) + Lena (Take) → Divorce (Talaq lena)!

1049.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1049.exampleEn: Every registered student must attend the morning orientation session
1049.shortcutEs: Asistir a (Ad- To + Sistere Stand = Stand present [Assist]!) | Acudir (Come promptly to aid/event!) = Attend!

1050.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1050.exampleEn: The whole family will gather together in the dining room for lunch.
1050.shortcutEs: Juntar (Latin root of "Junction / Join" together!) | Reunir (Twin of "Reunite"!) | Recoger (Re- + Coger Grab = Pick up together!) = Gather / Collect!
1050.shortcutHi: Ikattha karna (Built on Ek-saath One-together = Pile into one stack!) / Jama karna (Arabic loan used in Spoken Tamil ஜமா Jamaa = Collect/Deposit!) = Gather / Collect!

1051.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures

trans.es: 1. Join/append: Adjuntar / unir / pegar | 2. Separate/unfasten: Separar / despegar / soltar
trans.hi: 1. Join/append: Jodna / lagana | 2. Separate/unfasten: Alag karna / hatana

1051.exampleEn: Remember to attach your updated resume file to the job application email.
1051.shortcutEs:
1. Join/append: Adjuntar (Adjunct!) | Unir (Unite!) | Pegar (Stick like Pitch glue!) = Attach!
2. Separate: Separar (Separate!) | Despegar (Des- Un- + Stick!) | Soltar (Solution Unfasten!) = Detach!
1051.shortcutHi:
1. Join/append: Jodna (Link together — joint Jod!) / Lagana (Affix/Apply onto!) = Attach!
2. Separate: Alag karna (Set apart!) / Hatana (Move aside/Remove!) = Detach!
1051.hiDevanagari: 1. Join/append: Jodna / lagana | 2. Separate/unfasten: Alag karna / hatana

1052.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1052.exampleEn: It is completely unacceptable to insult someone based on their background.
1052.shortcutEs: Insultar (Twin of English "Insult"!) | Ofensa (Twin of English "Offense"!) = Harsh verbal attack = Insult!
1052.shortcutHi: Be-izzati karna (Be- Without + Izzat Honor = Strip away dignity!) / Gaali dena (Gaali Curse swear-word + Dena Throw!) = Insult!

1053.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1053.exampleEn: Older brothers often playfully tease their younger siblings at home.
1053.shortcutEs: Burlarse ("Burlesque" mocking joke — play prank on!) | Molestar de broma (Molestar Bother + de Broma as a joke!) = Tease!
1053.shortcutHi: Chhedna (From Chhed Poke/Bore — playfully poke ribs to annoy!) / Chidhana (From Chidh Snappy irritation — mimicking till they twitch!) / Satana (Sanskrit Sata trouble — bugging playfully like little mosquito!) = Tease!

1054.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1054.exampleEn: Do not try to flatter the manager just to gain an unfair promotion.
1054.shortcutEs: Adular (Same root as English "Adulate" — butter up with excessive praise!) | Halagar (Sweet-talk ego — picture someone melting under sweet Halwa praise!) = Flatter!
1054.shortcutHi: Makkhan lagana (Idiomatic gem: Literally "Spread Butter" — buttering someone up!) / Chaploosi karna (Smooth "Cheap-Applause" sycophant talk — Chaploos!) = Flatter!

1055.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs

trans.hi: Chugli karna / idhar-udhar ki baatein karna

1055.exampleEn: It is unkind to spread rumors and gossip about your coworkers.
1055.shortcutEs: Chismear / chisme (Latin Schisma Split/Tale-bearing rumor [Schism]!) | Cotillear (Busybodies chirping idle secrets!) = Gossip!
1055.shortcutHi: Chugli karna (Persian Chugli Whispering behind someone’s back!) / Idhar-udhar ki baatein karna (Here-there idle chatter!) = Gossip!
1055.hiDevanagari: Chugli karna / idhar-udhar ki baatein karna

1056.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs

trans.es: 1. Console person: Consolar / reconfortar | 2. Physical ease: Comodidad / confort
trans.hi: 1. Console person: Tasalli dena / dilasa dena | 2. Physical ease: Aaram

1056.tamil: 1. ஆறுதல் கூறு (Console person) / 2. வசதி / சௌகரியம் (Physical ease)
1056.exampleEn: She sat by her crying friend to comfort her with gentle words.
1056.shortcutEs:
1. Console: Consolar (Console!) | Reconfortar (Re- + Con- + Fortis Make strong again!) = Comfort (Verb)!
2. Physical ease: Comodidad (Commodity!) | Confort (Comfort!) = Comfort (Noun)!
1056.shortcutHi:
1. Console: Tasalli dena (Arabic Tasalli Calm soothing!) / Dilasa dena (Persian Dil-asa Rest the heart!) = Comfort (Verb)!
2. Physical ease: Aaram (Persian Aram [Tamil ஆறாமம் Ease!] Calm relief!) = Comfort (Noun)!
1056.hiDevanagari: 1. Console person: Tasalli dena / dilasa dena | 2. Physical ease: Aaram

1057.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1057.exampleEn: The enthusiastic crowd cheered loudly when our home team scored a goal.
1057.shortcutEs: Aplaudir (Twin of English "Applaud"!) | Animar (Inject fiery Anima spirit — "Animate" the crowd!) = Cheer / Applaud!
1057.shortcutHi: Taaliyan bajana (Taali Palm clap — Tamil தாளம் Thaalam! + Bajana Play rhythm!) / Hausla badhana (Hausla Morale + Badhana Lift up!) = Cheer / Applaud!

1058.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1058.exampleEn: The teacher praised the student for her creative and thorough essay.
1058.shortcutEs: Alabar (Vulgar Latin Alapare Brag/Exalt openly!) | Elogiar (Greek Eulogia Well-spoken tribute [root of Eulogy]!) = Praise!
1058.shortcutHi: Tareef karna (Arabic Ta’rif Making known one’s fine qualities + Karna Do!) = Praise!

1059.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1059.exampleEn: It is easy to criticize others, but much harder to offer helpful solutions.
1059.shortcutEs: Criticar ≈ Pointing out every tiny flaw like a harsh film critic! = Criticize!
1059.shortcutHi: Burai karna ≈ From Bura (Bad) → Pointing out bad flaws → Criticize (Burai karna)!

1060.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1060.exampleEn: Never mock someone who is trying their best to learn something new.
1060.shortcutEs: Burlarse ≈ Think "Burlesque" (mocking comedy satire) + de (of) → Poke fun at someone = Mock (Burlarse de)!
1060.shortcutHi: Mazaak udana / khilli udana ≈ Mazaak (Joke) + Udana (Make fly at someone's expense) = Mock!

1061.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1061.exampleEn: A truly skilled person does not need to boast about their talents.
1061.shortcutEs: Presumir (Twin of "Presume" — puff chest presuming superiority!) | Alardear (Origin in Arabic Al-ard = Parading army trophies noisily in review!) = Boast!
1061.shortcutHi: Deeng maarna (Beat a loud booming "Ding-Dong" drum about yourself!) / Phenkna (Slang: Literally "Throwing" tall whopper lies!) = Boast!

1062.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1062.exampleEn: You should apologize immediately if you make a mistake that hurts someone.
1062.shortcutEs: Disculparse (Dis- Clear away + Culpa Fault/Blame = Ask pardon!) | Pedir perdón (Pedir Beg + Perdón "Pardon"!) = Apologize!
1062.shortcutHi: Maafi maangna ≈ Maafi (Spoken Tamil மாஃபி / மன்னிப்பு = Pardon!) + Maangna (Ask/Beg) = Apologize (Maafi maangna)!

1063.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs

trans.hi: Madad karna / saath milkar kaam karna

1063.exampleEn: All team members must cooperate fully to finish the project before deadline.
1063.shortcutHi: Madad karna (Madad Aid + Karna Do!) / Saath milkar kaam karna (Saath Together + Milkar Joining + Kaam Work!) = Cooperate!
1063.hiDevanagari: Madad karna / saath milkar kaam karna

1064.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1064.exampleEn: Never betray the confidence and trust that your closest friends place in
1064.shortcutEs: Traicionar ≈ Stabbing an ally in the back (same root as "Treason"!) = Betray!

1065.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1065.exampleEn: Students who cheat on examinations face serious disciplinary penalties.
1065.shortcutEs: Engañar (Fool someone!) | Estafar (Swindle con-job!) | Hacer trampa (Set a sneaky Trap!) = Cheat / Deceive!
1065.shortcutHi: Dhokha dena (Prakrit Dhokha Illusion/Betrayal + Give!) / Ullu banana (Literally "Turn someone into an owl/fool"!) = Cheat / Deceive!

1066.category: Category 52: Physical Interaction, Flirtation & Social Gestures
1066.exampleEn: The dedicated doctors battled tirelessly throughout the night to save lives.
1066.shortcutEs: Batalla (Twin of "Battle"!) | Combate (Twin of "Combat"!) | Lucha (Wrestling struggle — famous Mexican wrestling "Lucha Libre!") = Battle!
1066.shortcutHi: Ladai (Built on verb Ladna = Physical clash/fight!) / Jung (Persian word for epic war!) / Sangharsh (Sam- Together + Gharsh Clash/Friction = Intense struggle!) = Battle!

1067.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1067.exampleEn: Close your eyes and imagine a peaceful quiet beach with crystal clear
1067.shortcutEs: Imaginar / imaginarse ≈ Painting vivid daydream worlds inside your mind! = Imagine!

1068.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1068.exampleEn: Can you guess how many jellybeans are inside this glass jar?
1068.shortcutEs: Adivinar ("Divine" unseen riddle — guess!) | Suponer (Twin of "Suppose"!) | Asumir (Twin of "Assume"!) = Guess / Suppose / Assume!
1068.shortcutHi: Andaaza lagana (Arabic/Persian Andaaz Measure + Lagana Estimate!) / Maan lena (Maan Accept mentally + Lena Take = Assume!) = Guess / Assume!

1069.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs

trans.es: 1. Verb - perceive: Notar / darse cuenta de | 2. Noun - written warning: Aviso / cartel
trans.hi: 1. Verb - perceive: Dhyan jaana | 2. Noun - written warning: Notice / khabar

1069.exampleEn: Did you notice the subtle change in her hair color this morning?
1069.shortcutEs:
1. Perceive: Notar (Twin of "Note"!) | Darse cuenta de (Darse Give oneself + Cuenta Account = Realize!) = Notice!
2. Warning: Aviso (Root of "Advise" bulletin!) | Cartel (Wall "Placard / Cartel" sign!) = Written Notice!
1069.shortcutHi:
1. Perceive: Dhyan jaana (Dhyaan Tamil தியானம் Focus + Jaana Go onto!) = Notice!
2. Warning: Notice (English loan "Notice" pinned on board) / Khabar (Arabic news/alert bulletin — Spoken Tamil கபர்!) = Written Notice!
1069.hiDevanagari: 1. Verb - perceive: Dhyan jaana | 2. Noun - written warning: Notice / khabar

1070.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1070.exampleEn: Scientists observe animal migration behavior carefully through satellite
1070.shortcutEs: Observar (Twin of English "Observe"!) | Mirar con atención (Mirar Look + con Atención with full Attention!) = Observe!
1070.shortcutHi: Ghaur se dekhna ≈ Ghaur (Arabic deep focused gaze — remember "Ghaur farmaiyega!" = Pay close attention!) + Dekhna (Watch) = Observe!

1071.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1071.exampleEn: I did not recognize my old school classmate after twenty long years.

1072.category: Category 53: Social Communication, Conflict & Reasoning Verbs
1072.exampleEn: The witness was asked to identify the suspect from a line of photographs.
1072.shortcutEs: Identificar ≈ Matching a fingerprint to its exact owner's ID card! = Identify!
1072.shortcutHi: Pehchan karna ≈ Pehchan (Recognition/ID mark) + Karna (Do) → Spot who or what it is → Identify (Pehchan karna)!

trans.es: 1. Evaluate merits: Evaluar / juzgar | 2. Court magistrate: Juez
trans.hi: 1. Evaluate merits: Parakhna | 2. Court magistrate: Judge

1073.tamil: 1. மதிப்பீடு செய் / ஆராய் (Evaluate merits) / 2. நீதிபதி (Court magistrate)
1073.exampleEn: Do not judge a person's character based solely on their outward appearance.
1073.shortcutEs:
1. Evaluate: Evaluar (Twin of "Evaluate"!) | Juzgar (Twin of "Judge"!) = Evaluate!
2. Magistrate: Juez (From Latin Judex — origin of "Judge / Judicial"!) = Judge!
1073.shortcutHi:
1. Evaluate: Parakhna (True jewel-tester rubbing gold on touchstone — Paaras/Parakh test!) = Evaluate / Judge!
2. Magistrate: Judge (English loan "Judge" holding courtroom gavel!) = Judge!
1073.hiDevanagari: 1. Evaluate merits: Parakhna | 2. Court magistrate: Judge

trans.es: 1. Guide path: Dirigir / guiar | 2. Straightforward adjective: Directo / recto
trans.hi: 1. Guide path: Raasta dikhana / aage le jaana | 2. Straightforward adjective: Seedha

1074.exampleEn: A police officer stood at the busy junction to direct heavy morning traffic.
1074.shortcutEs:
1. Guide: Dirigir (Twin of "Direct"!) | Guiar (Twin of "Guide"!) = Direct / Guide!
2. Straight: Directo (Twin of "Direct"!) | Recto (Twin of "Rectilinear / Straight"!) = Straightforward!
1074.shortcutHi:
1. Guide: Raasta dikhana (Raasta Path + Dikhana Show!) / Aage le jaana (Aage Ahead + Le jaana Lead!) = Direct / Guide!
2. Straight: Seedha (Sanskrit Siddha = Unbent straight arrow line!) = Straightforward!
1074.hiDevanagari: 1. Guide path: Raasta dikhana / aage le jaana | 2. Straightforward adjective: Seedha

1075.exampleEn: She knows how to handle difficult customer complaints with calm patience.
1075.shortcutEs: Manejar (Mano Hand = Handle/Steer!) | Lidiar con (Grapple in arena!) | Sobrellevar (Carry burdens!) = Handle / Cope!
1075.shortcutHi: Sambhalna (Hold steady/Balance under load!) / Jhelna (Absorb/Endure tough impact!) = Handle / Cope!

1076.exampleEn: Cacti can survive in hot arid deserts with very little water.

trans.es: 1. Steer clear: Evitar / esquivar | 2. Stop from happening: Prevenir / impedir
trans.hi: 1. Steer clear: Bachna / taalna | 2. Stop from happening: Rokna / bachav karna

1077.tamil: 1. தவிர் / ஒதுங்கு (Steer clear) / 2. தடு (Stop from happening)
1077.exampleEn: Drink plenty of water to avoid getting dehydrated on hot sunny afternoons.
1077.shortcutEs:
1. Steer clear: Evitar (Inevitable!) | Esquivar (Sidestep dodge [Eschew]!) = Avoid!
2. Stop happening: Prevenir (Pre- Before + Venire Come [Prevent]!) | Impedir (Impede!) = Prevent!
1077.shortcutHi:
1. Steer clear: Bachna (Keep oneself safe!) / Taalna (Push off/Defer aside!) = Avoid!
2. Stop happening: Rokna (Halt/Block!) / Bachav karna (Safeguard against!) = Prevent!
1077.hiDevanagari: 1. Steer clear: Bachna / taalna | 2. Stop from happening: Rokna / bachav karna

trans.hi: 1. Allow: Ijaazat dena | 2. Prohibit: Mana karna / rok lagana

1078.exampleEn: The rules do not permit smoking inside the public hospital building.
1078.shortcutHi:
1. Allow: Ijaazat dena (Arabic Ijaazat = Official permission + Dena Give!) = Permit!
2. Prohibit: Mana karna (Mana Refusal/No — Tamil மனம் / தடை!) / Rok lagana (Rok Block + Lagana Impose!) = Forbid!
1078.hiDevanagari: 1. Allow: Ijaazat dena | 2. Prohibit: Mana karna / rok lagana

1079.exampleEn: My grandmother always insists on cooking extra food for visiting family.
1079.shortcutEs: Insistir (Twin of English "Insist"!) | Empeñarse (En- Into + Peña Rock = Lock yourself stiff as rock!) = Insist!
1079.shortcutHi: Zidd karna (Zidd Iron obstinacy + Karna Do!) / Zorr dena (Zorr Force/Push + Dena Give = Press hard!) = Insist!

1080.exampleEn: Crop harvests depend heavily on receiving adequate rainfall throughout the
1080.shortcutEs: Depender de (Twin of English "Depend on"!) | Confiar en (Twin of English "Confide / Rely on"!) = Depend / Rely!
1080.shortcutHi: Bharosa karna (Sanskrit Bhar-Aasha = Solid pillar of trust!) / Par tikna (Par Upon + Tikna Stand/Rest solidly balanced!) = Depend / Rely!

1081.exampleEn: Please do not bother the doctor while he is performing an examination.
1081.shortcutEs: Molestar (Root of English "Molest / Annoy"!) | Fastidiar (Root of English "Fastidious" fussiness!) | Perturbar (Twin of English "Perturb"!) = Bother / Disturb!
